analysis: The PR is documentation-only: it changes docs/provider/troubleshooting.md and docs/threat-model.yaml. No executable code, protocol, key handling or authorization logic is touched. In troubleshooting.md, the 'Last updated' date moves to 2026-11-02. The quarantine row (head line 151) now also covers a release rolled back with `darkbloom update --rollback`. A new row (head line 152) tells operators to run `darkbloom update --rollback` when a release regresses and to leave automatic updates on. In threat-model.yaml (patch hunk at head lines 1887-1893), a new mitigation entry for the operator rollback is added, with status implemented. It says the rollback is the same journaled rollback under the same update lease, with the same predecessor verification and the same single-slot exact-version quarantine. It also refuses an installed bundle that differs from the recorded release and never rolls back one Mac of a cluster pair. This relates to T-043, the watchdog rollback authority entry, and to TB-003. The base file excerpt shows only the first ~472 lines, and the changed hunk sits around line 1884. The surrounding T-043 context, including the other mitigations and the threat's own wording, was not visible. The new mitigation claims are documentation of behavior, and I could not verify them against the Swift source (UpdateRecoveryState.swift, the update command), which is not in the batch. I identified no security regression. One residual question for integration: whether the code actually enforces the stated rollback properties (the same lease, predecessor signature verification, and the refusal on a bundle mismatch or cluster pair). The documentation claim is only as good as the implementation, which was not supplied. I also could not check whether the rollback command is deliberately exposed to an unprivileged same-user operator, or how it relates to T-043's replaceable-binary concern.
